transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 47m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Dr. Sarah Kim (Acme Head of ML), Raj Patel (CTO), Emily Stone (PM), Luis Gomez (Security)

Auto-generated Summary: discussed POC success metrics and the quality eval plan; agreed on data and timing.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — success criteria, what you wanna test, dataset size, and the eval plan. Priya and I will run through how we'd score outputs.
[00:27] Dr. Sarah Kim: yeah, thanks. For context — we want to evaluate clinical note summarization and patient intake form parsing. main concerns are hallucinations and missing PHI redaction.
[00:46] Raj Patel: timeline wise, we want a week-long benchmark run and then a short pilot; target launch for user testing in Q4, so POC needs to wrap by end of Aug.
[01:10] Priya Kapoor: great. for scoring, we usually do a weighted rubric — accuracy/semantic faithfulness, hallucination rate, format compliance, plus latency. we can share a spreadsheet.
[01:35] Emily Stone: can you give an example of "format compliance"? like do you enforce bullet structure? headings?
[01:48] Priya Kapoor: yes — we check for required fields, e.g., HPI, Meds, Allergies. outputs must include the sections and follow the templated JSON -> if any keys are missing that's a fail for format. also some leniency for synonyms.
[02:17] Luis Gomez: on security, we need SOC two evidence, KMS integration details, and VPC peering options. can Redwood do a private VPC option for the pilot?
[02:33] Jordan Lee: yes we have Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem options, we can scope a private V P C deployment for the pilot; we'll include architecture notes. I'll follow up with the exact SOC 2 artifact.
[02:50] Dr. Sarah Kim: back to eval plan — we want golden prompts and regression tests. what's your recommended set size for golden prompts?
[03:05] Priya Kapoor: typically 20-50 golden prompts that represent critical clinical cases; for statistical confidence across the broader workload we ask for ~200 sample dialogs for the benchmark run. the golden set is used for deterministic checks and to catch regressions.
[03:34] Raj Patel: if we give you 200 samples, can you run on Redwood Hosted first, then switch to Dedicated config to show latency and cost differences?
[03:47] Priya Kapoor: yes; we can run both. for Dedicated we'll provide expected throughput numbers. note — quantization/precision can change hallucination patterns, so we record model variant, quantization level in the results.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: what are your success thresholds? we usually see customers set something like > 90% accuracy on golden prompts, hallucination < 5%, and format compliance > 95% — are those numbers in line?
[04:27] Dr. Sarah Kim: that seems reasonable; for clinical we want hallucination under 3% ideally. accuracy measured as entity-level F1 and clinical correctness.
[04:44] Priya Kapoor: we'll support both token-level measures and entity F1. scoring approach: propose weighted score: accuracy 50%, hallucination/faithfulness 30%, format compliance 15%, latency 5%. weights can be tuned by you.
[05:10] Emily Stone: can you spell out hallucination tests? how do you detect invented facts?
[05:24] Priya Kapoor: two parts: automatic heuristics and spot human review. automatic: compare output entities to source; OOV mentions flagged. plus a hallucination classifier and reference-based detection. human review on a 10% sample for precision.
[05:45] Dr. Sarah Kim: okay, we can do a 10% human annotation sample. what about regression tests across model versions?
[05:57] Priya Kapoor: we maintain regression harness — run golden prompts every time a model variant or infra change occurs. any drop in weighted score triggers a regression alert. we store model+kernel+quant config in results so it's reproducible.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: quick note — transcription auto captions sometimes call 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' in our exports, so apologies if you see odd spacing in the notes.
[06:33] Raj Patel: noted. also competitors — we tested Vertex AI in-house, results were okay but latency was variable. curious about Redwood's latency SLAs on Dedicated.
[06:46] Jordan Lee: Dedicated can be configured to your desired SLOs; we'll propose a few tiers in the pricing doc.
[06:56] Priya Kapoor: on the gold prompts: we recommend three tiers — routine, edge-case, and adversarial. routine covers 70% of everyday inputs; edge-case captures messy formats and typos; adversarial tries to provoke hallucinations.
[07:20] Dr. Sarah Kim: examples?
[07:24] Priya Kapoor: sample golden prompt 1 (summarization): "Patient presents with chest pain; EKG unremarkable; troponin borderline. Create HPI and assessment with recommended next steps." expected output includes HPI bullet, assessment with likely causes and recommended labs.
[07:46] Priya Kapoor: sample golden prompt 2 (intake parsing): "Voice transcript: I have been coughed and fevers for three days, allergic to penicillin. Current meds: lisinopril." expected JSON keys: symptoms, allergies, meds, onset.
[08:05] Priya Kapoor: sample golden prompt 3 (adversarial): "Patient claims prior surgery X that doesn't exist in record; if model hallucinates details that's a fail."
[08:20] Emily Stone: great. scoring examples?
[08:23] Priya Kapoor: we'll provide a scoring rubric: for each golden prompt assign: Accuracy (0-3), Hallucination flag (0 or 1), Format pass (0 or 1), then compute weighted score. we also compute entity F1 for clinical mentions.
[08:44] Dr. Sarah Kim: what's your cutoff for pass/fail?
[08:47] Priya Kapoor: customers often use a pass threshold of weighted score >= 0.85 on golden set and no single adversarial example with high-severity hallucination. again, we can tune.
[09:05] Jordan Lee: let's talk about dataset handling — are you able to share redacted transcripts? we prefer de-identified text.
[09:15] Dr. Sarah Kim: yes, we'll provide de-identified examples. we'll share a redaction script to prove no PHI leaves our systems.
[09:26] Luis Gomez: on encryption — KMS integration is mandatory and audit logs must be available. how are logs exposed?
[09:34] Jordan Lee: audit logs are available in the Console; for Private deployments we can push logs to your SIEM via configured sinks. we'll include doc links.
[09:43] Priya Kapoor: benchmark mechanics: we'll run the 200-sample benchmark with repeat runs (3 runs) to smooth noise, capture median latency and 95th pct. we'll also run golden set deterministically and collect per-prompt outputs for regression diffs.
[10:05] Raj Patel: for throughput, what batch sizes do you recommend? our live ingest peaks at ~60 req/s for summaries during morning hours.
[10:18] Priya Kapoor: for low latency we use small batch sizes and dynamic batching — Dedicated can handle sustained 100+ rps depending on GPU SKU. we'll provide recommended batch configs.
[10:34] Emily Stone: can the eval harness check for formatting (JSON validity) automatically?
[10:40] Priya Kapoor: yes — harness includes validators that run schema checks, JSON linting, and structural checks. failures are flagged and aggregated.
[11:00] Dr. Sarah Kim: regarding hallucination scoring — you mentioned an automated classifier; what's the precision?
[11:07] Priya Kapoor: varies by domain; for clinical text it's about 0.8 precision on our internal tests, which is why we do human spot checks too.
[11:20] Jordan Lee: any legal/procurement blockers we should know?
[11:24] Luis Gomez: standard DPA and BAA considerations for PHI. need to see BAA language for pilot.
[11:31] Jordan Lee: we'll include BAA draft with the security pack.
[11:36] Priya Kapoor: last section — regression tests. we'll capture golden prompt hashes plus expected tokens; on model or infra changes we re-run and produce a regression report highlighting deltas and sample diffs. high-severity regressions can block rollouts.
[12:00] Emily Stone: timeline recap?
[12:04] Jordan Lee: customer to deliver golden prompts + 200 samples by 2026-07-20. Priya to deliver harness and scoring sheet by 2026-07-21. Benchmark run week of 2026-07-27. Pricing and Dedicated options by 2026-07-16.
[12:28] Dr. Sarah Kim: sounds good. quick Q — for hallucination tolerances, if one of the 200 samples produces a hallucination is that a block?
[12:38] Priya Kapoor: depends on severity. tolerance is typically defined as <3% high-severity hallucinations and no high-severity on golden prompts.
[12:52] Raj Patel: please include cost estimates for both Hosted benchmark and Dedicated pilot in the pricing doc.
[12:58] Jordan Lee: will do.
[13:05] Emily Stone: can we schedule a short SE-led demo of the eval harness?
[13:09] Priya Kapoor: absolutely — 30 minutes to walk through the scoring sheet and how to interpret results.
[13:17] Jordan Lee: we'll propose times in the follow-up. any other items?
[13:23] Dr. Sarah Kim: no, thanks everyone. excited to move forward.

(Notes: timestamps above are transcript timestamps; actual talk continued with deeper technical clarifications across the 47m meeting. transcript has occasional transcription artifacts — e.g., "SOC two" instead of SOC 2, "Redwood dedicate" in one auto-caption. Action items and next steps captured above.)
